testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a backing maneuver you will perform on the basic control skills test?
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test includes straight line backing, offset back/right, offset back/left, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Both systems in a dual air brake system share:
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the air compressor breaks, neither system will work.

questions.question: Cargo inside a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be secured
Should be stacked no more than three feet high
Should be secured to prevent movement
Should have the heaviest items on top of lighter items

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be secured to prevent movement
questions.explanation: Cargo must be secured to keep it from moving during transport. Load cargo to keep the vehicle's center of gravity low and balanced.

questions.question: If transporting 30 feet of cargo on a flatbed trailer, you should use a minimum of ____ to restrain the cargo.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo must have a minimum of two tie-downs.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Is a good way to save time
Is required to watch the cargo

questions.explanation: Avoid eating, drinking, or smoking while driving. Anything that takes your attention away from driving is a distraction.

questions.question: When looking under your vehicle's hood during a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Use the parking brakes and/or chock blocks
Leave the vehicle in a low gear

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the parking brakes and/or chock blocks
questions.explanation: Before inspecting under a vehicle's hood, set the parking brake and/or put chock blocks under the wheels.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within:
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems in about 45 seconds.

questions.question: When inspecting cargo, the driver should ensure all of the following, except:

options.text: The cargo is heavier at the top than the bottom

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is heavier at the top than the bottom
questions.explanation: When inspecting cargo, make sure it is balanced and properly secured. Keep the load weight as low as possible to prevent rollovers. Do not overload the trailer.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you should:

options.text: Create your own route to show your driving skills
Bring a passenger to ride with you

questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, follow the examiner's directions. The examiner will never ask you to drive unsafely.

questions.question: To use the stab braking method in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until they roll, then repeat
Apply the brakes halfway while keeping the wheels rolling
Fully apply the brakes, lock the wheels, and hold the pedal down until the vehicle stops

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until they roll, then repeat
questions.explanation: The stab braking method involves fully applying the brakes until they lock. Then release the brakes until the wheels start rolling. Repeat this process.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, you should:
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, shift to a low gear. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster as you travel downhill.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:

options.text: Press the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly.
Push the brake pedal down quickly.
Press the brake pedal repeatedly, but do not hold it down all the time.
Use the same amount of brake force every time you slow down or stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal slowly and smoothly every time you slow down or stop. The amount of brake force you need depends on how fast you are going and how quickly you need to stop.

questions.question: Backing up with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.
There may be extra weight in the front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. If you must back up, use a helper if possible.

questions.question: In the basic vehicle control skills test, you will:

options.text: Be tested on how well you operate the vehicle.
Have to remove the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be tested on how well you operate the vehicle.
questions.explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, you will be tested on how well you operate your vehicle. You will be asked to move forward, back up, and turn within a marked area.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Always shift to a lower gear before entering a curve. Slowing down before the curve helps you control the vehicle better while turning.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, make sure the spring brakes turn on automatically when:
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, make sure the spring brakes turn on automatically when air tank pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. You can test this by blocking the wheels and releasing air from the brake system by pressing and releasing the brake pedal. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve should pop out and spring brakes should turn on.

questions.question: To get a CDL, you must be at least:
questions.explanation: In Pennsylvania, you must be at least 18 years old to get a CDL. To drive a commercial vehicle across state lines, you must be at least 21.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:
questions.explanation: When crossing railroad tracks during the driving skills test, do not stop, shift gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the crossing.

questions.question: After driving under an overpass during the skills test, you may be asked to remember:

options.text: If there was a shoulder near the road.

questions.explanation: If you drive under an overpass during the driving skills test, your examiner may ask you to remember the posted clearance or height of the overpass.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles require ____ to change gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions use double clutching to change gears. You should release the gas, push in the clutch, and shift to neutral at the same time. Then release the clutch and let the vehicle reach the right speed. Next, push in the clutch again, shift gears, and release the clutch while speeding up at the same time.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Let you drive faster than normal.
Let you follow other vehicles more closely than normal.
Let you drive less carefully than normal.
Does not reduce your stopping distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not reduce your stopping distance.
questions.explanation: ABS helps you keep control when braking hard. It does not make you stop shorter.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Brake shoes with oil or grease on them
Brake pads with no oil or grease on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake pads with no oil or grease on them
questions.explanation: Bad brake signs include cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are worn dangerously thin. Clean pads are normal and safe.

questions.question: In very hot weather, how can you prevent your tires and engine from overheating?
questions.explanation: Faster driving makes your engine and tires hotter. In hot weather, slow down to help prevent overheating.

questions.question: If your brakes pull to one side when you use them, what does it mean?

options.text: The brakes need to be checked.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes need to be checked.
questions.explanation: A vehicle that pulls to one side when braking has a brake problem. Fix it before driving. Driving an unsafe vehicle breaks federal and state laws.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Help prevent the wheels from locking up
Stop a vehicle from accelerating going uphill
Stop a vehicle from accelerating going downhill

questions.correctAnswerText: Help prevent the wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: ABS prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: When driving, what should you look at?

options.text: Keep your eyes on the road ahead.
Look only at the front and right side.
Look only at the front and sides.
Look at the front, sides, and rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the front, sides, and rear.
questions.explanation: Safe driving means knowing what is happening all around your vehicle. Watch the road ahead and check your mirrors often to see what is beside and behind you.

questions.question: During the driving test, you will be tested on gear use. What should you NOT do?

options.text: Use a gear that makes the engine rev too much.
Forget to shift in an intersection.

questions.explanation: During the driving test, pick a gear that does not make the engine rev too much. Avoid grinding gears. Do not shift while turning or in an intersection.

questions.question: How should you do a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Do it the same way every time.
Only do it on sunny days.
Skip it if the vehicle seems fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do it the same way every time.
questions.explanation: Always do your pre-trip inspection the same way. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you do not skip anything.

questions.question: What do the air storage tanks do?

options.text: Hold air for only one braking cycle.
Hold enough air for several braking cycles if the compressor fails.
Hold air only during an emergency.
Hold air for more than 1,000 braking cycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for several braking cycles if the compressor fails.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough air so brakes can be used several times if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: If you get a traffic ticket in your personal car, what must you do?

options.text: The officer will tell your employer.
Your CDL will not be affected because it was in your personal car.
Tell your employer within six months.

questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction, no matter what vehicle you were driving. Parking tickets do not count.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Complete the test without a moving violation.
Obey all traffic signs and signals only when other cars are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey all traffic signs and signals only when other cars are present.
questions.explanation: You must drive safely during the on-road test. Wear your safety belt. Obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws. Complete the test without an accident or moving violation.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill:

options.text: Use your brakes the whole way down.
Shift into a higher gear to slow down.
Shift into a lower gear to slow down.
Put the truck in neutral to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear to slow down.
questions.explanation: On a steep hill, use the engine to slow down by shifting to a lower gear. Use your brakes only to help. This stops your brakes from overheating.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is an encroachment?

options.text: A driver putting the vehicle in neutral and using the parking brake.
The vehicle touching a boundary line.
A driver completing an exercise correctly.
An applicant trying to bribe the examiner.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle touching a boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment is when your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during an exercise. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: In very hot weather, check your tires regularly because:
questions.explanation: Hot weather makes air expand. Your tire pressure can get too high. If this happens, stop and let your tires cool. Do not let air out, as pressure will drop too much when the tires cool.

questions.question: During the straight line backing exercise, how many times can you exit the vehicle to check its position?
questions.explanation: During the straight line backing exercise, you can exit your vehicle to check its position only one time.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: Always drive so your vehicle can stop:

options.text: Within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within the distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Drive at a speed where you can stop completely within the area of road you can see in front of you.

questions.question: If you lose your driving privileges for your personal vehicle:

options.text: Your CDL will not be affected.
Your CDL will be limited to daytime driving only.
Your CDL will be limited to Class B vehicles.

questions.explanation: If your driving privileges are revoked, canceled, or suspended for traffic violations in your personal vehicle, you will lose your CDL.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights. Use them even during the day.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, make sure that:

options.text: Emergency exits are hard to open.
Emergency exit warning devices work properly.
Emergency exits cannot be opened from inside the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Emergency exit warning devices work properly.
questions.explanation: Check that emergency exit warning devices work. All emergency exits should open easily, be in good condition, and close securely from inside.

questions.question: After passing the CDL written test, how long must you wait before taking the skills tests?
questions.explanation: After you get your commercial learner's permit, you must wait at least 15 days before you can take the skills test.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a type of retarder?
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow a vehicle and reduce brake wear. The four types of retarders are exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric.

questions.question: During a walk-around inspection, brake drums should have no cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check the brake drums before each trip. Do not drive if a brake drum has a crack larger than one half the width of the friction area.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a tire problem to check for?

options.text: Radial and bias-ply tires used together
Recapped tires on the front of a school bus
All tires are made by the same company

questions.correctAnswerText: All tires are made by the same company
questions.explanation: During an inspection, check for low or high air pressure, excessive wear, cuts, tread separation, tires touching each other, mismatched sizes, mixing radial and bias-ply tires, damaged valve stems, and regrooved or recapped tires on the front of a school bus. It does not matter which company made the tires.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted?

options.text: When you are standing next to the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Check mirrors before starting your trip. If your vehicle has a trailer, mirrors can only be adjusted correctly when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: After changing a tire, why should you stop after a short distance?

options.text: To check that the wheel nuts are tight.
To check that the tire has enough air pressure.
To confirm the correct tire was changed.
To check that no other tire was damaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check that the wheel nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop after a short distance to re-check that the wheel nuts are tight.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.
Be careful because the brakes may fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not apply the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: During the skills test, if you must stop before turning, you should:

options.text: Stop after the stop line for a better view.
Keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: Stop smoothly behind the stop line. Keep your front wheels straight and do not let your vehicle roll. Stop where you can still see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: After driving over a bridge during the skills test, you may be asked to recall what?

options.text: The color of a sign you passed.
How many traffic lanes were on the bridge.
If there was a crosswalk on the bridge.

questions.explanation: During the on-road skills test, if you drive over a bridge, the examiner may ask you to recall the bridge's posted weight limit.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?

options.text: Try to get out of their way.

questions.explanation: If confronted by an aggressive driver, try to get out of their way. Avoid eye contact and ignore their gestures. Do not speed up or try to challenge them.
